Reducing stress is a highly personal endeavor, and what works for one person may not be effective for another. However, there are a few methods that have consistently proven to be effective for a wide range of people. One of the most universally endorsed ways to combat stress is through regular physical exercise. Engaging in activities like running swimming, or even a brisk walk can release endorphins, the body's natural stress relievers. For example, someone who incorporates a daily jog into their routine often finds that this time allows them to clear their mind and focus on something other that their daily worries. this physical exertion not only improves mood but also promotes better sleep, which is crucial for stress management.

Another method for alleviating stress is through mindful practices such as mediation or yoga These activities help to center the mind, promote relaxation, and enhance one's ability to cope with stressors. Practice yoga can help release physical tension and improve mental clarity. Similarly, mediation encourages a state of calm and mindfulness.

Engaging in hobbies or creative pursuits is another valuable way to reduce stress. Activities such as reading, gardening, painting, or playing a musical instrument can provide a much-needed escape from the pressure of everyday life. For example, someone who enjoys gardening may find solace in tending to their plants. Experiencing a sense of accomplishment and peace as they watch their garden flourish.

In conclusion, while there are many ways to reduce stress, physical exercise, mindfulness practices, and engaging in hobbies each offer unique benefits that can help individuals manage their stress more effectively.

Stress, though a negative, is a normal part of our lives. While it can be true that we can say that were not stressed when we were younger, I'm sure we will all come to a point of experiencing noticeable stress. Over time, when stress is not handled well, it accumulates and can be detrimental to different aspects of our lives. Accumulated stress can affect our productivity, decision-making, and various components of our well-being, the physical, emotional, and mental health. These are why we need to be equipped with ways to manage stress. The best ways I know are: proper sleep; regular exercise; and other positive habits.

Sleep is a crucial necessity of our body. It gives us the energy to face on another day! While we sometimes consider this element to be optional, thinking that productivity is equal to time spent on a task, we just end up adding more stress to ourselves. It is not optional! And we really shouldn't just sleep for the sake of sleeping, we need to have regular eight hours of sleep time. Studies continue to back up that sleep simply just adds to our longevity. We live longer when we sleep good!

Another thing is regular exercise. It has been considered to be a better alternative to anti-depressant drugs! When we exercise, even for a good 30 minutes a day, and not just sweating because it's hot where we live but our hearts beating like crazy, we've done a great deal for our well-being. We don't just add up to our muscles but also to our brain power! Exercising may seem to be stressful, but it's the other way around. It combats stress. Keeping exercise a regular thing in our routine makes it easier and more fun.

Now, as you can see, the two things I've mentioned are not just the activity themselves. It's not just sleeping, but sleeping properly. It's not just bursting out on an exercise, but making it regular. What's a word for this way of including an activity regular in our lives? Yes, a habit! Positive habits make it so that we can fill our days with a pattern. When we do the same good things over and over again, we will not accumulate stress doing them! An example would be setting a time of the day for homeworks. If we do it an hour in the morning and then we study at night the next day, we won't be on a good rythm. But if we decide on a time suitable for us, and we do it for a week, and then a month, or even a whole semester? It will be so easy to do.

These things are very specific ways to manage and reduce stress. And it all boils down to discipline. As stress is consistently present in our lives, we need to be disciplined to also be consistent in doing the ways to prevent the accumulation of it. Whatever good practice we have for ourselves will do, just be disciplined with it. Living a disciplined life makes a great life. Even with difficult circumstances or stressful happenings, we will be able to make it meaningful. That is, if we are disciplined.

Classes have always been part of the learning process, starting from pre-school up to college. They foster a learning environment that allows a learner to develop their ability to gain knowledge in different fields of study. In a typical university, students attend classes that are relevant to their major course of study. Additionally, some may take other classes that are not as relevant but helps them to gain a broader knowledge across multiple disciplines. While attending classes are important to develop a student's understanding and learning, some may find the requirement to attend classes to be demanding and overwhelming. Because of this, some argue that classes should only be an option for students. Although I acknowledge the struggles students face in attending these classes, I disagree that they should not be mandatory.

Classes are structured in a way that students are guided with a teacher or instructor to learn specific areas related to their course of study, resulting in a gradual increase of their knowledge in the field over time as they take more classes. By having the option to skip these classes, students may acquire gaps in their learning and may eventually seek other sources to fill this gap. It can be detrimental to a student's learning process if the sources are not as effective as being able to participate in a class gives. The freedom to choose whether to attend a class or not may lighten the workload of university students, especially those juggling with extracurricular activities, jobs, or other responsibilities, however this also reinforces the fact that having a requirement to attend classes can enable the students to develop their ability to balance their time between classes, activities, and other things.

All students have different circumstances, schedules, and workloads, but learning should not become a second priority in their lives. Not being required to attend classes may enforce this idea, which can minimize the development and growth a student should be getting during their time in a university. Attending classes should be mandatory to not only allow the student to learn more and expand their knowledge in their chosen field of study, but to help them develop new skills such as time management and prioritization.
